text.headline: Dias rounds Cape of Good Hope
text.text: Bartolomeu Dias became the first European to sail around the southern tip of Africa, proving a sea route to Asia was possible and opening the Age of Exploration.

events.notes: This achievement encouraged Portugal to continue eastward exploration toward Asia, inspiring da Gama's later voyage to India.

text.headline: Columbus reaches the Caribbean
text.text: Christopher Columbus, funded by Spain, landed in the Bahamas — believing he had reached Asia. This contact began sustained European colonization of the Americas.

events.notes: Columbus made four voyages to the Americas. His arrival initiated the Columbian Exchange — the transfer of plants, animals, and diseases between hemispheres.

text.headline: Treaty of Tordesillas
text.text: Spain and Portugal divided the non-European world along a meridian, giving Portugal Africa/Asia and Spain the Americas (except Brazil). Other European powers ignored this treaty.

events.notes: Brokered by Pope Alexander VI, the treaty shaped colonial boundaries for decades — though France, England, and the Netherlands never recognized its authority.

text.headline: Cabot explores North America
text.text: John Cabot, sponsored by England, reached Newfoundland, establishing England's claim to North America — a foundation for later English colonization.

events.notes: Cabot's voyage gave England its primary legal claim to North America, later cited when establishing Jamestown and other colonies.

text.headline: Da Gama reaches India
text.text: Vasco da Gama completed the sea route to India, establishing direct Portuguese trade with Asia and breaking the Venetian/Ottoman monopoly on Eastern trade goods.

events.notes: Portuguese spice trade profits funded further exploration and made Lisbon one of Europe's wealthiest cities during the early 1500s.

text.headline: Balboa sees the Pacific
text.text: Vasco Núñez de Balboa crossed Panama and became the first European to see the Pacific Ocean from the Americas, dramatically expanding European understanding of world geography.

events.notes: Balboa's sighting confirmed that a vast ocean separated the Americas from Asia — a discovery that motivated Magellan's circumnavigation attempt six years later.

text.headline: Cortés invades the Aztec Empire
text.text: Hernán Cortés landed in Mexico. By 1521, with the help of thousands of Indigenous allies opposed to Aztec rule, he conquered Tenochtitlán, ending the Aztec Empire.

events.notes: Disease, especially smallpox, killed millions of Indigenous people before and during the conquest. The fall of the Aztec Empire opened central Mexico to Spanish settlement.

text.headline: Verrazano explores North America
text.text: Giovanni da Verrazano, sailing for France, explored the eastern coast of North America from the Carolinas to Canada, establishing French claims to the continent.

events.notes: Verrazano sailed into what is now New York Harbor and Narragansett Bay. His voyage laid the groundwork for France's future settlements in Canada.

text.headline: Pizarro conquers the Inca Empire
text.text: Francisco Pizarro captured Inca Emperor Atahualpa and, despite a ransom of gold and silver, executed him. The Inca Empire collapsed, giving Spain access to vast silver mines.

events.notes: Inca silver, mined at Potosí (present-day Bolivia), flooded European markets and funded Spanish power for a century — but also triggered inflation across Europe.

text.headline: Cartier explores the St. Lawrence
text.text: Jacques Cartier sailed into the St. Lawrence River, claiming what became New France (Canada) for the French Crown and making contact with Iroquois and Huron nations.

events.notes: Cartier's voyages established France's claim to the interior of North America, eventually leading to Quebec City (1608) and a vast fur-trade empire.

text.headline: First Roanoke Colony
text.text: England's first attempt to plant a permanent colony in North America, on Roanoke Island (present-day North Carolina). The colony failed — the 'Lost Colony' mystery remains.

events.notes: When a supply ship returned in 1590, all 115 colonists had vanished. The word 'CROATOAN' carved on a post remains the only clue to their fate.

text.headline: Jamestown founded
text.text: The first permanent English settlement in North America. Nearly half the settlers died the first winter; tobacco cultivation eventually made it profitable and established plantation agriculture.

events.notes: Jamestown's survival depended on Powhatan Confederacy trade. By the 1620s, tobacco profits drove demand for enslaved labor — foreshadowing the plantation economy.

text.headline: Hudson explores New Netherland
text.text: Henry Hudson, sailing for the Dutch East India Company, explored the Hudson River, establishing Dutch claims to what became New Amsterdam (present-day New York City).

events.notes: The Dutch founded New Amsterdam in 1626. England seized it in 1664 and renamed it New York — but Dutch cultural influence (Brooklyn, Harlem, Wall Street) endures.
